title: From Exodus to Eucharist
blurb: Follow the Passover lamb and the manna in the wilderness to the bread Jesus gives at the Last Supper and in John 6.

steps.title: The Night of Passover
steps.intro: On the eve of the exodus, each household sacrifices a lamb and marks its doorposts with the blood. The meal is eaten in haste, and Israel is told to keep the day as a lasting memorial.

quote.text: Pascha, as they say who know, and who have explained to us what to read, meaneth “Passover.” When then the Lord’s Passion was about to come, the Evangelist, as though he would use this very word, saith, “When the hour was come that Jesus should pass over to the Father.”

steps.question: Which saving acts of God do you keep as a regular memorial, and how do you mark them?

steps.title: Bread from Heaven
steps.intro: In the desert, the hungry people complain and God provides manna each morning. They are to gather only what they need for the day. The New Testament later reads this gift in light of Christ.

quote.text: That manna came from heaven, this is above the heavens; that was of heaven, this is of the Lord of the heavens; that was liable to corruption, if kept a second day, this is far from all corruption

steps.question: What would it mean to depend on God daily for what you need, and not store up for yourself?

steps.title: Behold the Lamb
steps.intro: John the Baptist points to Jesus and calls him the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world. The title echoes the Passover lamb and the suffering servant, and prepares the way for John's account of the Passion.

quote.text: They brought and presented a suckling lamb to the Paschal Lamb, a first-born to the First-born, a sacrifice to the Sacrifice, a lamb of time to the Lamb of Truth.

steps.question: What does it mean for you that Jesus is both the one who offers and the one who is offered?

steps.title: I Am the Bread of Life
steps.intro: After the loaves are multiplied, the crowd asks for a sign like the manna. Jesus replies that his Father gives the true bread from heaven, and that he himself is the bread of life.

quote.text: “This is the bread that cometh down from heaven;” that by eating it we may live, since we cannot have eternal life from ourselves.

steps.question: What hunger in your life do you hope Christ alone can satisfy?

steps.title: Eating His Flesh
steps.intro: Jesus says the bread he will give is his flesh for the life of the world, and that whoever eats his flesh and drinks his blood has eternal life. The Church has long read this passage in a Eucharistic sense.

quote.text: We live then by Him, by eating Him; that is, by receiving Himself as the eternal life, which we did not have from ourselves.

steps.question: How does the idea of receiving Christ as life, and not as a reward, change how you come to Communion?

steps.title: This Is My Body
steps.intro: At the Passover meal on the night before he died, Jesus takes bread and a cup and says, "This is my body" and "This is my blood of the covenant." He gives the old feast a new meaning.

quote.text: Consider therefore the Bread and the Wine not as bare elements, for they are, according to the Lord’s declaration, the Body and Blood of Christ; for even though sense suggests this to thee, yet let faith establish thee.

steps.question: What helps you approach the Eucharist with faith rather than judging by appearances alone?

steps.title: One Bread, One Body
steps.intro: Paul asks whether the cup and the bread are a sharing in the blood and body of Christ, and concludes that many who share one loaf are one body. Communion joins believers to Christ and to each other.

quote.text: “For why speak I of communion?” saith he, “we are that self-same body.” For what is the bread? The Body of Christ. And what do they become who partake of it? The Body of Christ: not many bodies, but one body.

steps.question: Who in your parish or family is hard to see as part of the same body, and what could you do?
